titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 146, the pylons, part 1
part: Spell 146 — the pylons: the first six pylons (Plate 11)
about: Spell 146 takes the dead man through the pylons (sbḫt) of the house of Osiris. At each pylon he says the pylon's titles, greeting it as a goddess, and names its one doorkeeper. On Ani's papyrus the spell runs along the lower register of Plates 11 and 12, below Spell 147; this part gives the first six pylons, all on Plate 11, and Budge numbers the lines afresh at each pylon. Many of the titles and all of the doorkeepers' names are doubtful, and the copy has several slips of the scribe's.

sentences.l: what-is-said · when · arriving · at · pylon · first
sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the first pylon.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these six words in red. This unit opens Spell 146 and its first pylon, on the lower register of Plate 11, under Spell 147. Budge starts his line numbers again at 1 at each pylon; the first pylon runs over his lines 1 to 8, with his numeral 9 printed inside its last word. ḏdt is the cobra ḏ, the hand d, t and plural strokes, as in the title of Spell 1: the passive participle of ḏd 'say' used as a noun, 'what is (to be) said' (Budge: t'eṭet). ḫft 'when, at the time of' (the placenta ḫ, the horned viper f and t) stands before the infinitive spr 'arriving', the rib spr (coded F42, approximate) with r and walking legs, and r 'at', as at the first gate of Spell 147. sbḫt 'pylon, portal' is the folded cloth s, b, ḫ and t, with two classifiers: a tall tower with a flared cornice and a doorway at its foot, the gateway of a temple (coded O16, approximate; the type has no exact sign), and the house. tpyt 'first' is the head tp with p and t, the ordinal, feminine to agree with sbḫt; its y is not written. Where the gates of Spell 147 have three keepers each, each pylon of Spell 146 has one doorkeeper, and the dead man must know the pylon's own titles, which he says to it as to a goddess.

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani, true of voice:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red; the rest is black. ḏd in N 'said by N' brings in the speech, as in Spell 147: ḏd is the cobra and the hand, printed as one sign, and in is a reed and water n. wsir 'the Osiris' is a low seat (coded Q2, approximate) and the eye, without the god classifier: the dead man named as an Osiris. Ani's name ends in the squatting man with a flail (A52); mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is the plinth and the oar, without the sickle, as often on this papyrus.

sentences.i: Lady of dread(?), high of walls,
sentences.n: The speech begins: the dead man greets the pylon by its titles. nbt 'lady (of)' is the basket nb with t, the feminine of nb 'lord', before a direct genitive. The next word is the bolt s, a bird not identified, its neck coiled in a loop over its back (coded G38, approximate), ꜣ and w, with the sparrow and plural strokes. Budge reads setau ('terrors'), taking the bird with ꜣ for tꜣ; the sparrow is the classifier of bad things, so a word of dread fits, but the bird and so the word are doubtful. qꜣt 'high' is the hill-slope q, ꜣ and t, with the man with raised arms and a tall narrow sign (coded Y1a, approximate; Budge's numeral 2 stands before the word) as classifiers: the adjective qꜣ in the feminine, agreeing with the pylon. sbtyw 'walls' is s, b, t and two strokes y, with a wall with ticks on both sides (coded O36, approximate), a small wedge (coded N21, approximate) and plural strokes: the plural of sbty 'enclosure wall, rampart' (Budge: sebti). qꜣt sbtyw 'high of walls' is the adjective followed by the noun it applies to, as English says 'high-walled'.

sentences.i: chief, lady of slaughter(?), who foretells words,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes r, n and t with the man with hand to mouth; read srt 'who foretells', as Budge's footnote has it (sert), with the bolt s in place of water n. In his text line Budge prints dots for this word, and the correction rests on his footnote: srt is the feminine participle of sr 'foretell, make known', and the hand-to-mouth classifier marks a word of speech. ḥryt-tp 'chief' is the face ḥr with r and t, and the head tp with its stroke: ḥryt, the feminine of the nisba ḥry 'who is upon', with tp 'head', 'she who is at the head'. nbt 'lady (of)'. ḫbḫbt is ḫ and b written twice and t, with the low sign coded U15, not read: a reduplicated word, taken with Budge as 'destruction, slaughter' (χebχebet); the word is not otherwise known in these parts, and its sense is doubtful. ḏdw 'words' is a tall tapering stick (coded U28, approximate) for ḏ, the hand d and w, with the man with hand to mouth and a stroke: a plural noun from ḏd 'say' (Budge: t'eṭṭu, though only one hand is printed).

sentences.l: who-drives-back · the-storm · who-rescues · the-one-gone-far(?) · for · the-one-who-comes(?)
sentences.i: who drives back the storm, who rescues the one who has gone far(?), for the one who comes(?).
sentences.n: ḫsf 'who drives back' is the spindle-and-viper sign ḫsf with the low sign U15, a participle. nšny 'the storm' is water n, the pool š, n and two strokes y, with U15, as in Spell 17 (Budge: neśeni, 'destroyers'). nḥm 'who rescues' is water n over a bowl with three points on its rim (coded W10, approximate), taken as carrying ḥm, because Budge's footnote spells the word with the same bowl followed by m; under it stand two long lines (coded N36, approximate) and U15, which may together be the arm with a stick, the classifier of force, and are not read. wꜣy is a loop with a tall curved stroke (coded V4, approximate: the lasso wꜣ), with ꜣ, two reeds y and walking legs (Budge's numeral 3 is printed inside it): taken as a participle of wꜣi 'go far', 'the one who has gone far'. Budge renders it 'destruction', which the walking legs do not support. n 'for' is water n alone, the only word of Budge's line 3, and iy, the sign ii (M18) with a reed, two strokes y and walking legs, the participle of ii 'come', 'the one who comes', fills his line 4 (his English there, 'the traveller along [the way]', is printed in braces). How the last words hang together is not clear: n could also be 'of', and the whole is doubtful. Budge's second footnote prints another papyrus's version of these words; it is not part of Ani's text.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Neruyt.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s 'the name of its doorkeeper', as in Spell 147, but iry is spelled out here: a reed, r and two strokes y, with the seated herdsman with his stick (A47, approximate; Budge's numeral 7 is printed before him) as classifier. Budge's groups àri and āa-s are joined here into one word. A tall narrow sign (coded Y1a, approximate; perhaps the door-leaf, or an upright form of the ꜥꜣ sign) is not read; the hatched bar coded O29 (approximate) gives ꜥꜣ 'door', over the low sign U15; a kneeling man with a raised arm (after Budge's numeral 8) is the classifier of a person; and the bolt is ·s 'its', the pylon's. The sentence has no verb: 'the name of X (is) Y'. The name is water n, r and w, two reeds y and t (Budge's numeral 9 after it), a hunched vulture (coded G14), U15 and the seated god: nrwyt, perhaps from nrw 'terror', which takes the vulture as its classifier, 'the Terrible one' (?) (Budge: Neruit). The first pylon ends here.

sentences.l: what-is-said · when · arriving · at · pylon · second
sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the second pylon.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these words in red. This unit opens the second pylon, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the second pylon runs over his lines 1 to 7. The words are those of the first pylon; Budge's numeral 2 is printed inside sbḫt, and its tower sign is drawn here as a wall with a frieze of small hooked strokes on top (coded O16, approximate). snnwt 'second' is the pot nw over two strokes, the numeral two (sn): the ordinal snnw, its feminine t not written.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. The words are those of the first pylon, here with sš 'scribe', the scribe's palette, water pot and pen case. Budge's numeral 4 is printed inside Ani's name.

sentences.i: Lady of the sky, mistress of the Two Lands,
sentences.n: nbt 'lady (of)', its t restored by Budge inside his square brackets. pt 'the sky' is p and t with the sky sign. ḥnwt 'mistress (of)' is the wick ḥ and an open cup (coded W10, approximate), the cup that serves for ḥnwt, with t; the wick announces the ḥ. tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt, is the flat land sign written twice for the dual, with two small wedges (coded N21, approximate) as classifiers. These are titles of the great goddesses, here given to the pylon.

sentences.l: who-devours · lady · of-mankind · exalted(?) · above · person · every
sentences.i: she who devours, lady of mankind, more exalted(?) than anyone.
sentences.n: nsbyt 'she who devours' is water n over an angular hooked sign (coded F20, approximate), taken as the tongue ns, then s, b, two reeds y and t, with the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of eating: the feminine participle of nsb 'lick, devour' (Budge: nesbit). nbt 'lady (of)', its t again restored inside Budge's brackets. tmmt 'mankind' is t, the sledge tm, m and t, with a man, a woman and a stroke: tmmw 'all people' in a feminine collective form (Budge: tememet). The next word is t, n, the pot nw and w, then a compound sign not identified, an H-shaped post (coded U38, approximate) joined to a crested bird with raised wings (coded G24, approximate), and t with the roll. It is read here as ṯnwt, from ṯni 'be distinguished, raised above', with t for ṯ; the same word is written with ṯ at the sixth pylon. r 'above, than' is the r of comparison. bw nb 'everyone' is b and w, the noun bw 'place', and the basket nb 'every', here followed by a man and a woman: 'every person'. Budge makes the comparison an exclamation ('how much greater … than all peoples'); the reading of ṯnwt rests on a sign not identified and is doubtful.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper is Mes-Ptah.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s as at the first pylon (Budge's numeral 7 is printed inside rn). Budge's groups àri and āāau-s are joined here into one word: iry spelled with a reed, r, two strokes and the herdsman; then the narrow sign coded Y1a (not read); a rod with a lozenge knob, lying flat, taken as the ꜥꜣ sign (O29, approximate), with the arm ꜥ, ꜣ and w; the hatched bar O29 again over U15 (neither read); the kneeling man; and the folded cloth ·s 'its'. The w may make the plural ꜥꜣw 'door-leaves'; the sense, 'doorkeeper', is the same (Budge: āāau-s, 'its door'). The name is the three fox skins ms with s, then p, t (restored by Budge inside his square brackets) and the wick ḥ, with the seated god: ms-ptḥ, perhaps 'Born of Ptah' (?), naming the god of Memphis (Budge: Mes-Ptaḥ). pw 'it is', p and w, closes a sentence without a verb: 'the name … is Mes-Ptah'. The second pylon ends here.

sentences.l: what-is-said · when · arriving · at · pylon · third · of · the-house · of-Osiris
sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the third pylon of the house of Osiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the words up to nt in red; pr wsir is black. This unit opens the third pylon, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the third pylon runs over his lines 1 to 7. ḫmtnwt 'third' is three strokes, the numeral three (ḫmt), with the pot nw and t: the ordinal ḫmtnw, feminine. nt 'of' is the genitive in its feminine form, agreeing with sbḫt. pr 'house' is the house sign with its stroke, and wsir the low seat and the eye: the pylons are the gateways of the house of Osiris.

sentences.i: Says the scribe Ani, true of voice:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes mꜣꜥ-ḫrw twice; read it once. Budge's numeral 6 and a blank space on the papyrus (he prints '[⅜ in. blank]') stand between the two writings, and he marks the second (sic); it is not rendered. in, a reed and water n, is written in red under its own short line, with no ḏd before it: in followed by a name is the verb 'says', 'says N'. Ani is not called the Osiris at this pylon. Budge's numeral 5 is printed inside his name.

sentences.i: Lady of the offering table, great of offerings,
sentences.n: nbt 'lady (of)'. ḫꜣwt 'altar, offering table' is a lotus leaf on its stem (M12) for ḫꜣ, with ꜣ, t and w, and a tall stand with a three-pronged top (coded R1, approximate) as classifier (Budge: χaut). ꜥꜣt 'great' is the sign coded O29 (approximate; here a thin shaft with a lozenge end) for ꜥꜣ, with ꜥ, ꜣ and t and the roll: the adjective in the feminine. ꜥbt 'offerings' is the arm ꜥ crossing the leg b, and t, with a frame filled with zigzag lines (coded R3, approximate: an offering table), the roll and a stroke (Budge: ābt). ꜥꜣt ꜥbt 'great of offerings' is again an adjective with the noun it applies to, like 'high of walls' at the first pylon.

sentences.l: the-companion(?) · of-god · every · sailing-upstream · to · Abydos
sentences.i: companion(?) of every god, who sails upstream to Abydos.
sentences.n: The first word is the folded cloth s, a sign like the ankh (coded S34, approximate) where the hoe mr would be expected, m and r, with a bird lying flat (coded G38, approximate) and t. Budge reads smert, 'beloved'; it is taken here as smrt, the feminine of smr 'companion', the courtier's title 'Friend', a word built on mri 'love'. The two senses are near, and the bird is not a usual classifier of either; the reading is doubtful. nṯr nb 'every god' is the flag with the seated god, and the basket nb after its noun. ḫnty 'sailing upstream' is a frame with three uprights (coded W17, approximate) for ḫnt, with n, t and two strokes y, and a boat with its sail up as classifier: a participle of ḫnti 'sail upstream, fare south', which the north wind makes possible. Who sails is not said; the participle may describe the pylon. r 'to' is restored by Budge inside his square brackets. ꜣbḏw 'Abydos' is the sign coded S34 (the house ruling for ꜣb) with b, the hills ḏw and the town sign, as in Spell 147: the holy city of Osiris, upstream of the Delta and of Memphis.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Sebaq.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s as before. Budge's groups àri and āa-s are again joined into one word, here with the narrow sign Y1a (not read), the hatched bar O29 for ꜥꜣ, the kneeling man and the folded cloth ·s, without U15. The name is s, b, ꜣ and the wedge q (printed small and raised), then an upright oval on a short foot pierced by an arrow (coded F29, approximate) and the seated god (Budge: Sebaq). If it is sbꜣq 'be bright' (?), the name would be 'the Bright one'; the arrow sign is not understood, and the name is doubtful. The third pylon ends here.

sentences.l: what-is-said · when · arriving · at · pylon · fourth
sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the fourth pylon.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these words in red. This unit opens the fourth pylon, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the fourth pylon runs over his lines 1 to 6. fdnwt 'fourth' is four strokes, two over two, the numeral four (fdw), with the pot nw and t, as at the fourth gate of Spell 147.

sentences.i: Says the Osiris, the scribe Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes in in red. As at the third pylon, in alone, 'says', with the name after it; here Ani is called the Osiris again, and his name is written without a classifier.

sentences.i: Mighty one of knives, mistress of the Two Lands,
sentences.n: sḫmt 'mighty' is the sceptre sḫm with m and U15 (not read): the adjective of sḫm 'be mighty' in the feminine, its t not written (Budge: seχem). dsw 'knives' is the hand d, the bolt s and w, with a curved knife (coded T30, approximate), a small wedge and plural strokes: the plural of ds 'flint knife'. 'Mighty of knives' is once more an adjective with its noun. ḥnwt 'mistress' is written here with the cup and t alone, without the wick; tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', each land sign with its small wedge.

sentences.i: who destroys the enemies of the Weary of Heart,
sentences.n: ḥḏt 'who destroys' is an upright with a round top and a crossbar entwined by a cobra (coded as the mace ḥḏ, T3, approximate, and the cobra ḏ), the crossed sticks, t and the sparrow: the feminine participle of ḥḏ 'damage, destroy', with the crossed sticks of breaking and the bird of bad things as classifiers (Budge: ḥet'et). ḫftyw 'the enemies' is ḫ, f and t with a kneeling man with an arm raised to his head (coded A14, approximate) and a stroke; the plural ending is not written, but the genitive after it is plural. nw 'of' is the pot nw with a stroke. wrd ib 'the Weary of Heart' is the swallow wr with r, the hand d, a seated figure with hanging arms (coded A7, approximate) and the sparrow, then the heart with its stroke and the seated god: wrd-ib, a name of the dead Osiris, as in Spell 1 (Budge: urṭ àb, 'Still-heart').

sentences.i: who makes the one in need(?) free of harm.
sentences.n: irt 'who makes' is the eye, r and t, the feminine participle of iri. The next word is the folded cloth s, a small box-like sign coded Aa18 (approximate) for sꜣ, ꜣ, r and t, with a hanging loop and a slanting stick (coded V6, approximate) and the man with hand to mouth: read sꜣrt, from sꜣr 'want, need', 'the one in need' (?). šwt is a tall feather bent at the top (coded H6, approximate) for šw, with w, t and the sparrow: šw 'empty, free (of)', in the feminine to agree with sꜣrt. m 'of, from' is the owl. iwt 'harm, wrong' is a recumbent young animal (coded E9, approximate), the sign iw, with w and the sparrow; its t is not written (Budge: āu). irt X šwt, 'who makes X free', puts the object between the verb and the word that says what it is made. Budge renders 'making the decree of dismissal of the needy from harm'; the reading of sꜣrt is doubtful.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Negau.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s with iry written by the herdsman alone, as in Spell 147, and an upright hatched sign coded O29 (approximate) for ꜥꜣ. The name is water n over a small stand with an angle inside it (coded W11) for g, ꜣ and w, with a bull and the seated god: ngꜣw, the word for the long-horned bull, which takes the bull as classifier, so perhaps 'the Long-horned Bull' (?) (Budge: Neḳau). The fourth pylon ends here.

sentences.l: what-is-said · when · arriving · at · pylon · fifth
sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the fifth pylon.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these words in red. This unit opens the fifth pylon, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the fifth pylon runs over his lines 1 to 6. diwnwt 'fifth' is five strokes, two over three, the numeral five (diw), with the pot nw and t, as at the fifth gate of Spell 147.

sentences.i: Says the Osiris, the scribe Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes in in red: a reed and a hooked forked sign coded W25 (approximate; the house reading for in), as in Spell 147. Ani's name ends here in a kneeling man with a raised arm (A1).

sentences.i: Fire, lady of the breath(?) of the nose,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes r, š, a reed and t with the nose; read šrt 'nose', with r and š changed round. The nose classifier (coded D19, approximate) leaves only a word of the nose; Budge reads the signs as they stand, reśàt, 'the nostrils'. ḫt 'fire' is the placenta ḫ and t with a tall flame (coded Q7, approximate) as classifier: the word for fire, here a title of the pylon (Budge: χet, 'Flame'). nbt 'lady (of)'. The next word is a clump of papyrus (M16) for ḥꜣ, with ꜣ and w, the roll and plural strokes: ḥꜣw, an abstract noun not identified; Budge renders 'breath', which suits the nose, and he is followed here with a query. The fire that is lady of the breath of the nose may be the pylon's burning breath, or the breath it gives; the sense is doubtful.

sentences.i: No one goes down to entreat her(?).
sentences.n: n 'not' is the arms held out (D35), the negative. hꜣ is the shelter h, ꜣ and walking legs: hꜣi 'go down', a sḏm·f with no subject written, 'one goes down' (Budge: ha, 'advance'). n 'for' is water n. The last word is s, the hand d, b and the wick ḥ, with a thin stick with an angled end (coded M3, approximate) and the man with hand to mouth, then t and w and the bolt ·s: sdbḥ, taken with Budge as 'entreat' (seṭebḥ), a causative from dbḥ 'ask for, require', with ·s 'her', the pylon; sdbḥ may instead be 'provide for, equip'. t and w, the ending of the sḏm·tw·f 'one …', would belong to the first verb ('one goes down'); written after sdbḥ, they might make it 'she is entreated'. The construction is not clear, and the unit is doubtful.

sentences.i: No one goes in to her while his head is (on him)(?).
sentences.n: n 'not' is the arms held out with water n as complement. ꜥq 'enter' is the bird ꜥq with q and walking legs, a sḏm·f with no subject written, 'one enters'. r·s 'to her' is r with the bolt ·s. wnn is the hare wn with water n twice, the verb 'be', and tp·f 'his head' is the head with its stroke and the viper ·f. Budge prints (sic) over the viper and leaves both words untranslated, with a dotted line. They are taken here as a clause of circumstance, 'his head being (on him)': no one goes in to her and keeps his head. With ·s for ·f it would be 'her head'. The sense is doubtful.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Hentyt-arqyu.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s, with the herdsman and the hatched sign O29 (approximate). The name, a single group in Budge's type (Ḥentet-Ārqiu), is the wick ḥ, a plant with three buds (coded M2, approximate) for ḥn, n, t, two strokes y and t, with U15 (not read); then the arm ꜥ, r, the wedge q, two reeds y and w, with a curling cord (coded V1, approximate), walking legs, the seated god and a stroke. ḥntyt is not identified; ꜥrqyw may belong with ꜥrq 'bind, swear' (?), for which the cord would be the classifier. The name is not understood. The fifth pylon ends here.

sentences.l: what-is-said · when · arriving · at · pylon · sixth
sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the sixth pylon.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these words in red. This unit opens the sixth pylon, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the sixth pylon runs over his lines 1 to 6. sisnwt 'sixth' is six strokes, three over three, the numeral six (sis), with the pot nw and t, as at the sixth gate of Spell 147.

sentences.i: Says the Osiris, the scribe Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes in in red. As at the fourth and fifth pylons; Ani's name ends in the kneeling man (A1).

sentences.i: Lady of brightness(?), great of roaring,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes m, h, ꜣ, h and t; read hmhmt 'roaring, the war-cry', with the owl m set before the first h and ꜣ where the second m belongs (Budge: hemhat, 'shoutings'). nbt 'lady (of)'. snk is the bolt s, water n and the basket k, with the sun as classifier (Budge: senk, 'light'); taken here as 'brightness' (?). The word is not otherwise known in these parts, and the sun shows only that it is a word of light or time, so the sense is doubtful. ꜥꜣt 'great' is the sign coded O29 (approximate; a thin shaft with a lozenge end) with t and the arm ꜥ: the feminine adjective, with hmhmt after it, 'great of roaring'. The roar is the battle cry of a fierce goddess.

sentences.i: Her length and her breadth are not known.
sentences.n: n 'not' is the arms held out. rḫ·tw is r and ḫ with a tall narrow sign (coded Y1a, approximate; the roll) as classifier, then t and w: the sḏm·tw·f of rḫ 'know', 'one knows', after n 'one does not know' (Budge: reχ-tu). ꜣw·s 'her length' is a hatched slab on an arch with curled ends (coded F40, approximate: the backbone sign ꜣw), two oblique strokes and the bolt ·s: ꜣw 'be long' used as a noun, 'length' (Budge: āu-s, 'her breadth'). wsḫ·s 'her breadth' is the cup wsḫ (W10, approximate) with ḫ and ·s (Budge: useχ-s). The pylon cannot be measured.

sentences.i: Her like has not been found since the beginning.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes š, ꜣ and s; read šꜣꜥ 'beginning', with s for the arm ꜥ. Budge prints (sic) after his transliteration śas and renders 'the beginning (?)'. n 'not', the arms held out. gm·n·tw is the ibis gm, water n, t and the quail chick w (Z7): the sḏm·n·f of gmi 'find' with the ending tw, 'one has found', after n 'one has not found' (Budge: qementu). qd 'form, likeness' is the builder's level qd (coded Aa28, approximate) with d, the pot nw (not read) and the roll (Budge: qeṭ, 'the like'). m 'since, from' is the sign Aa15. šꜣꜥ is a pool with three lotus flowers (M8) for šꜣ, with ꜣ, the s and the roll: m šꜣꜥ 'from the beginning', since the world was made.

sentences.i: A serpent is upon her.
sentences.n: iw, a reed and w, opens the statement and is not translated. ḥfꜣw 'serpent' is the snake (coded I14, approximate) alone, a sign that stands for the whole word, and a stroke restored by Budge inside his square brackets (Budge: ḥefu, 'a worm'). ḥr·s 'upon her' is the face ḥr with its stroke and the folded cloth ·s. iw with a noun and ḥr·s says where the thing is: a serpent lies on the pylon, as its guard.

sentences.l: not · is-known · the-greatness(?) · has-been-born-(it) · before · the-Weary-of-heart
sentences.i: Its greatness(?) is not known; it was born before the Weary of Heart.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the face ḥr with its stroke where the heart ib belongs; read wrd-ib 'the Weary of Heart', the name of Osiris at the fourth pylon. Budge prints (sic) over the face and transliterates urṭ-[àb]. n rḫ 'it is not known' is the arms held out, then r and ḫ with ꜣ (not read) and a stroke. The next word is enclosed whole in Budge's square brackets, restored: the hobble ṯ (coded V13), n, the pot nw and w, the same compound sign not identified as at the second pylon (coded U38 and G24, approximate), the roll and a stroke: ṯnw, from ṯni 'be distinguished, raised up', here a noun, 'greatness' (?) (Budge: θennu, '[how great]'). ms·n·tw is the three fox skins ms with s, water n, t, w and a stroke: the sḏm·n·f of msi 'give birth' with the ending tw, 'one has borne (it)', 'it was born' (Budge: mes-entu). ẖr ḥꜣt 'before' is the butcher's block ẖr with r, and the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t and a stroke: 'in front of', which may also be 'before' in time. wrd-ib is the swallow, r, the hand d and the figure with hanging arms, then the face, the stroke and the seated god. The serpent was born in the presence of the dead god, or before him in time.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Sematy.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s as before. The name is the bolt s and the sickle mꜣ, drawn across the vulture ꜣ as one sign, t and two strokes y, with the lung-and-windpipe sign smꜣ (F36) and the seated god: smꜣty (Budge: Semati). smꜣ is 'unite', the sense of the sign F36, and a word of the same sound is 'slay', so perhaps 'He of uniting' or 'the Slayer' (?); the name is doubtful. The sixth pylon ends here; the seventh follows in the next part.
